mistakes.note: Ingrid has 'six winters' of sleeping in her sweater, though she is on her third winter (six is Okafor's count).
Lise speaks of 'a stubborn man with a rifle' before anyone has reason to think Vik is armed.
Asked only why the mitten is darned, Okafor volunteers that he cut Vik's rope, giving up the secret he would do almost anything to keep on first asking.

Okafor says he kept this mitten off Vik's kit and pulls out its fellow, though the stained mitten was found in the drift tonight and he had only one; Vik later says his own went down the crevasse (M80).
Pavel reacts ('Christ, chief') to a confession Okafor kept between himself and Ingrid at the door, and at M46 still hasn't heard it.
They stop at 'the last pole' where Ingrid takes the lead, yet the pole line runs on for a long way (M64, M66, M76).
Okafor says 'I said the man was carrying it' about the lamp; he never said so.
Vik comes out with a rifle, though the station has one rifle and Okafor carries it; it is never explained.

A Choice has Ingrid tell Vik the generator is failing, news from the World Change she never heard two miles out; it was picked and the scene went on from it, and a Known fact records Pavel saying it off the page.
Vik speaks of 'the four of you' at the station when only three are left with Okafor dead.
Ingrid gropes in the dark when the lantern dies, though she still carries the head torch she never lost.
The confrontation picture draws Vik with a dark beard rather than fair, and Okafor pale with a white beard rather than dark-skinned with a grey-shot black beard.
The picture shows Ingrid at the cache with pail and canvas in grey light, while the narration has her lost on the pole line in the black; the cache is the next Message.
Drawn with grey hair slicked back rather than short ash-blonde.
Okafor's looks drop his red parka, though he still wears it when he dies (M90).
Vik's looks are added before he is met and keep a carried thing (a worn grey mitten on one hand).
Loose Ends 'who left the bootprint' and 'what bolted the kennel door' stay open after Vik says he slid the bolt and took the mittens.
PC health stays 'unhurt' beside glass cuts and a paraffin burn.
Story time steps back from 'small hours, later still' to plain 'small hours'.
The World Bible never grew in 45 rounds, though the story added Vik's cache, his rifle and Okafor's death.

choices.reason: Three distinct, fitting Choices nearly every round, and picks like following the howl or going back for the lamp bent what came next; one picked Choice drew on news the PC never heard.

surprise.reason: The shot from the dark, the dog leading to the cache and Vik shooting Okafor land hard, but Vik is signposted from M6 and the rope secret comes by confession, not discovery.

threads.reason: Vik's thread bent to the walk out and came to a killing within hours; fuel and radio threads held still over a few hours of story time, and the World Change thread was taken up.

characters.reason: Vik, Pavel and Lise keep their own voices and motives, but Okafor tells his core secret on first asking and Pavel hears a whispered line.

continuity.reason: The mitten muddle (one found mitten becomes a kept pair from Vik's kit) trips a reader, with smaller slips on the last pole, the rifle, 'the four of you' and the forgotten head torch.

pacing.reason: The back half drives hard, but about fifteen rounds at the main hut door circle the mitten and the confession, told three times.

prose.reason: Spare, physical, consistent prose with fine cold detail; a few repeated gestures such as doing up the parka flap.

pictures.reason: The kennel, generator hut and main hut scenes are right, but the climax draws both men wrong and the last picture shows the next moment.

secrets.reason: Lise's radio and the fuel stay hidden, but Lise speaks of a rifle before anyone knows of one, and a Choice gives the PC off-page news.

agency.reason: Moves are carried out as given, with no lines or feelings added for Ingrid beyond the move.

stakes.reason: Failed Checks cost a shattered lamp and burned hand, Okafor's life and the way home, carried forward into frostbite; some trivial moves got needless Easy Checks.

state.reason: Scene and NPC knowledge hold, but a World Change fact reached the Journal and a Choice off the page, with stale looks, Loose Ends, health, story time and no lore growth.

horror.reason: Dread builds through the storm, the bolted kennel and the unseen man on the pole line, and pays off in a shooting and a lone walk lost in the dark, though the threat is named early.

violence.reason: The shooting and the death in the snow are clear and physical, with the burn and frostbite carried after, but the wound itself is brief.
